biography.concept: Keeper of the titles for the cinema-vigil family — Ember-Touched (Igneous Menhirkin) Cosmic Linguist, T III, Initiation 13 (Act 3).
biography.notes: Indwimeir reads the credits. Every film the family remembers, Indwimeir can recite — cast, crew, the catering company — and treats the lists as scripture, because in the Hidden Vault a name said correctly still opens things. Ember-touched: the Igneous heat never left Indwimeir's hands, and the marquee letters are re-lit by them each dusk. Indwimeir is the one who taught the family the incantation and the one who will not say where it came from.

description.value:
"The land is not scenery. The land is a person. You are the version of it that finally stood up and walked over to complain."

You are not descended from the land. You are the land. A hex decided to become a person and the person is you. The standing stones on the ridge are distant cousins. The bedrock under the bunker is a grandparent. Mortals call you a Hex-Giant. You don't correct them.

Creature Type. Humanoid (Menhirkin). Size. Medium, but you count as Large for carrying capacity and the size of creatures you can shove or grapple. Speed. 6 squares

Heartstone (passive). A fragment of your home hex is literally inside you. While in any hex your Domain controls or has claimed: reroll the lowest die on Body checks, and you cannot be forcibly removed from the hex against your will (teleportation, banishment, forced march) without first being reduced to 0 Integrity.

Land Memory (1/Soma Break). Lay a hand on any surface older than you; the GM tells you one true thing the land remembers.

Living Rampart (1/Soma Break). Reaction — when a creature you can see targets an ally adjacent to you with an attack, the attacker rolls 3d10 keep lowest 2 on that attack roll.

Stonebound (passive). Reroll the lowest die on Body checks to resist being pushed, knocked Prone, or otherwise forcibly moved. Reroll the lowest die on Body checks to build, repair, or fortify structures, siegeworks, and defensive emplacements.

Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Violence marks and +20 Non-Lethal marks at campaign start.

description.value:
“Some stone was born yelling.”

Menhirkin (Igneous). You are new rock. The Shattering was your birthday. The land that stood up and began answering chose you because it wanted a mouth that remembered being molten. You run hot, you cool slow, and you are, structurally, still furious about something.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Menhirkin).
  • Size. Medium.
  • Movement. 6 squares walking.
  • Lineage Lean. Menhirkin does not grant fixed attribute bonuses; your background handles increases. Your heritage leans toward Violence in fiction and through Tier powers.

Menhirkin Core: The Land Stood Up

Shared across all Menhirkin heritages. Granted at character creation via the base ancestry item.

  • Stone Soul. You count as Large for carry, shove, and grapple despite your Medium frame. You reroll the lowest die on checks to resist being forcibly moved.
  • Hex Recognition. Once per scene, while you are on a natural surface you are directly touching, you may whisper a single question about the place. The GM answers with one true thing the land knows.
  • Slow to Wear. You reroll the lowest die on Body checks against Stress, long-duration physical wear, forced marches, climate exposure, and sustained labor. You do not tire the way softer things tire.
  • Heavy Presence. Your weight and settledness are perceptible. Creatures within 2 squares of you know you are there even if they cannot see you; you roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on Intrigue (Stealth) checks unless you are on or in stone.

Igneous Traits

  • Heat Memory. When you take thermal damage with the fire flavor, you may bank that damage. Before your next Soma Break, you may spend the banked heat as a bonus action to add +1d10 exploding thermal damage (flavor: fire) to your next weapon attack, unarmed strike, or grapple that connects.
  • Molten Bearing. You count fire, smoke, ash, and heated terrain as normal ground for the purposes of difficult terrain and footing. Contact with your bare skin singes paper and warms metal.

Domain Edge

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Violence marks and +20 Non-Lethal marks at campaign start.

description.value:
"Strike the clause. Insert your own. Reality reads from the top."

The Cosmic Linguist edits reality like text — meaning first, matter second. One currency now: Surge. The editor always has the next word, so you bank +1 Surge at the start of your turn (the old Resonance, Strain, and Editorial Authority pools are folded into this single pool).

The Edit (spent via Surge)

  • Emphasis (1) — your next Strike or manifestation hits for +Tier d6 (the word, underlined).
  • Stabilize (2) — you gain DR equal to Tier; your next cast resists counter / dispel (the sentence holds).
  • Impose a Reading (3) — a foe's next attack and its saves are rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2 (only one correct interpretation: yours).
  • Rewrite the Sentence (5) — a foe loses its reactions and rolls saves rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2; allies near you bank a reroll.

The Sentence endures as your signature stance — while held, the manifestation's primary target is bound by name and rolls its checks against you rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2.

description.value:
"See below. It changes everything above."

Doctrine: Prefer surgical changes with precise scope — a small note that produces a large consequence. You are strongest when the edit looks modest.

The Annotator wins in the margins. Your Surge spends are footnotes with teeth: shore up an ally's roll, pin a foe with marginalia it cannot ignore, and revise the whole passage at once.

Doctrine (spent via Surge)

  • Footnote (1) — an ally banks a reroll-lowest (a small note, a large consequence).
  • Marginalia (2) — a foe is Staggered and rolls its saves rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2.
  • Revision (5) — allies within 6 squares each bank a reroll-lowest (the whole passage, corrected).

The Edit — your four class Surge spends, from the ◆ Surge menu.

  • Emphasis (1) — your next Strike or manifestation hits for +Tier d6 (the word, underlined).
  • Stabilize (2) — you gain DR equal to Tier; your next cast explodes on 9–10 (the sentence holds).
  • Impose a Reading (3) — a foe's next attack and its saves roll 3d10 and keep the lowest 2. Only one correct interpretation: yours.
  • Rewrite the Sentence (5) — a foe loses its reactions and rolls saves rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2; allies near you bank a reroll.

These are the old Resonance channels spoken in the one currency: Surge. The Sentence (Initiation 11) endures as your signature stance on top of them.

"Magic is grammar. Reality is a draft."

You are a prepared, academic manifestant who edits meaning directly. You do not delegate power; you channel it raw.

Engine truth: your craft runs on Clarity (your casting pool, deeper than other paths), Noise (the lattice hears sloppy work), Surge (the editor's one currency — +1 at the start of your turn), and Blood Debt (reaching above your tier, discounted by your Discipline). The cast dialog's cost line is the truth.

An earlier draft of this class spoke of Resonance, Strain, and correspondence alignment. Those pools were folded into Surge — the fiction survives; the bookkeeping does not.

"I am not casting. I am editing."

Roleplay register, not rules. Choose the voice of your edits — Additive, Subtractive, Transformative, Referential, or Performative. Narrate every manifestation in your mode: it shapes how the working looks, sounds, and is remembered — never what it costs.

The cast dialog's cost line is the truth. (An earlier draft priced modes in Strain; Strain is retired.)

Initiation 1 — True-Name Touch. You bank +1 Surge at the start of each of your turns (max +2 a round). When you spend Clarity to manifest, you may name the target as part of the action. For the rest of the scene, extending that manifestation's Reach to the named target costs 1 less Surge / Blood Debt (minimum 0).

Discipline (passive): Reach discount −1 on Blood-Debt-reach. Skill rank +1 in two of: Occult, Lore, Insight.

Name a target as part of your manifestation. For the rest of the scene, extending that manifestation's Reach to the named target costs 1 less Surge (min 0).

Initiation 6 — Translation. 1/scene signature move: as a reaction to an ally completing a manifestation within Reach, transcribe it into your idiom. Until the end of the next round, you carry their effect at your tier cap, paying its upkeep from your Clarity. Your translation, your bill.

Discipline: passive Reach discount unchanged from Init 1; Translation itself is a 1/scene narrative power resolved at the table.

description.value:
(3rd Level)

You reduce misfire risk through formal preparation.

When you cast using:

  • Diagrams

  • Circles

  • Correspondence-correct timing

  • Proper ritual framing

Reduce misfire risk gained (GM adjudicated; typically by 1).

This applies only when the preparation meaningfully exists in fiction.

You are not suppressing risk.

You are managing it.

(3rd Level)

You annotate rituals with correspondence-perfect notes.

Effects

  • Ritual casting is faster or more stable (GM adjudicated).

  • Aligned rituals bank additional Surge.

  • Misaligned rituals generate a gentler misfire band than usual.

Your rituals are not safer because they are weaker.

They are safer because they are correct.

(6th Level)

You bank one prepared manifestation as a sigiled casting.

After deliberate preparation:

  • Store one prepared manifestation as an inscribed annotation.

  • Later, cast it quickly without losing the stored working until the stored version is discharged.

This does not remove misfire risk.

It front-loads stability.

You prepared yesterday so you can survive today.

Sure Recitation

You speak your workings cleanly, even under pressure.

Rules

On any manifestation cast roll, you may reroll the lowest die, keeping the new result if it is higher.

Requires: General — Tier 2+

⚙ Applies automatically: reroll the lowest die on every manifestation cast.

Scavenged Insight

Debris tells stories.

Rules

After a combat encounter, you may ask the GM one factual question about what the enemies were carrying, guarding, or afraid of.

✍ Table rule.
